title: Dry-run migration logbook: TF wrapup and compatibility experiments
summary: Notes and results from three dry-run migration experiments against customer-like environments, Terraform wrapper changes, compatibility test outcomes, and a concise rollback cookbook for private (VPC/on-prem) migrations.
content:
Purpose and context
This doc is the lab-style logbook for the September->February dry-run cycles where we validated: TF module changes, control-plane handshake upgrades, runtime KV schema migrations, and API adapter shim behavior. The goal: produce a minimally invasive migration pattern that can be run against customer staging fleets with clear gating metrics and deterministic rollback steps.

High level conclusions (one-paragraph)
- The minimal-safe path is a 3-stage approach: 1) preflight TF and proxy feature toggles; 2) staged runtime rollout with silent compatibility probes; 3) handoff + verification and then traffic cutover.
- Two high-risk items that need automation before GA: consistent KV cache snapshot/restore for heterogeneous nodes, and automated shim layer to translate legacy client headers for 72 hours post-cutover.

Experiment matrix (environments run)
- env-A (lab-small): 3 node on-prem cluster, 2x A100-equivalent simulation, 20k tokens/min synthetic load, TF module v0.9-wip applied. Purpose: validate TF change orchestration and node-level reconcile.
- env-B (customer-sim): VPC with private control plane (simulated CICD), mixed GPU types (A100 + T4), real traffic replay from customer X (redacted). Purpose: runtime KV migration and cache-hit behaviour under mixed latency.
- env-C (air-gapped): offline appliance build, manual artifact transfer, TLS/HSM integration enabled. Purpose: validate signed artifact delivery and offline upgrade flow.

Key artifacts changed in TF (notes for module owners)
- wrapper module: private_deployments/wrap_01.tf — added new resource "redwood_controlplane_migration" with lifecycle.create_before_destroy true and a reconcile_timeout variable. Rationale: avoid control-plane brief outages when migrating stateful CRs.
- outputs: preserved previous outputs but added outputs.migration_token and outputs.post_migrate_rev to enable idempotent redeploy.
- example module usage (appendix shows snippet). Keep IAM changes scoped and add a transient role.

Preflight checklist (automatable items in bold)
- Configuration diff run: confirm TF plan shows no resource replacement outside expected controlplane nodes.
- **KV snapshot:** run kv-backup --target=GCS --consistent=true and verify checksum across nodes.
- Network checks: all private endpoints resolvable, LUCI/HAProxy routing rule test (curl through proxy).
- **Shim binary smoke test:** start adapter with --dry-run and assert 0 translation failures for 10k requests.
- Monitoring hooks: add temporary trace tag migrate_id and enable debug logging for 1 hour post-cutover.

Compatibility probe pattern (safe probing)
- Silent probe mode: route 1% of traffic through upgraded runtime variant with header X-Redwood-Compat-Test: staging. Responses are logged but not returned to clients.
- Probe sizing: start 1rps per node, ramp to 20rps over 30 minutes while measuring latency P50/P90/P99 and error-rate.
- Golden criteria to promote: P99 degrade < 2x baseline AND 99.95% success on translation path AND no new 5xx spike in controlplane logs.

Observed results (by experiment)
- env-A: TF wrapper worked; create_before_destroy prevented transient control-plane restarts. KV snapshot restore time ~ 18s for small partitions. Shim translation latency added +6ms median.
- env-B: Mixed GPU scheduling exposed a KV hot-shard: hit-rate dropped ~14% when runtime variant was rolled to T4 nodes. Mitigation: shard-aware placement and temporary cache-warm strategy.
- env-C: Offline-signing process required adding an explicit certificate TTL step. Manual transfer times dominated overall maintenance window; recommend parallel file transfer step and a transfer-verification script.

Known failure modes and mitigations
- Failure: KV restore race causing stale KV reads after a pod restart. Mitigation: enforce pod annotation migrate_kv_block=true during rollout and drain traffic until restore_complete metric emitted.
- Failure: TF plan drifting because of IPAM allocations in customer VPC. Mitigation: create plan-lock resource and export IPAM allocations to state-external bucket.
- Failure: Legacy clients sending deprecated header X-Runtime-Id. Shim drop occurred causing 400s. Mitigation: shim now supports header aliasing and logs unmapped headers for 72h, then alerts.

Rollforward checklist (what to run during live migration)
1) Baseline snapshot and store (kv-backup + store sha256)
2) TF plan/apply using wrapper module with create_before_destroy enabled
3) Start 0.5% silent probes for 15 minutes, then 2% for 45m, then 10% for 60m if stable
4) Perform incremental KV upgrade on a single node, observe restore_complete and heatmap of cache-hit ratio
5) If any gating metric fails, trigger rollback plan (below)

Rollback cookbook (concise actionable steps)
- Trigger conditions: any of the golden criteria fail OR controlplane error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m OR KV restore time > 5x baseline
- Immediate actions:
  a) Remove upgraded variant from routing via selector: kubectl label nodes redwood/migrate=paused (or hit autoscaler exclude flag).
  b) Revert TF: terraform apply -var='migration_token=<prev>' -target=module.wrap_01 -auto-approve (this expects outputs.post_migrate_rev to be set).
  c) Restore KV snapshot: kv-restore --source=GCS://<bucket>/snap-<id> --force-consistent. Wait for restore_complete metric.
  d) Re-enable clients gradually and monitor P99.
- Postmortem steps: collect traces (trace:migrate_id), attach plan file, collect node-level /var/log/redwood/runtime.log and controlplane audit events. Create PD-rollback report within 24h.

Automation priorities before next run (requirements)
- Autotool to validate TF drift related to IPAM and to lock plan state automatically pre-apply.
- A small binary update for shim to emit header-mappings as structured logs and a k8s sidecar to tail these and feed into metrics.
- A KV warmup controller to prepopulate caches on new nodes before shifting traffic.

Test checklist (manual + automated testcases)
- Unit: tf module plan idempotency test (repeat plan 5x)
- Integration: full dry-run against env-B with traffic replay at 50% of production; must pass gating rules for 3h continuous window
- Chaos: simulate node restart during KV restore; expected: draining and restore completes, no 5xxs for >1 minute window post-restore

Appendix A: sample TF wrapper usage (copy/paste)
module "migration_wrap" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private_deployments/wrap_01"
  migration_token = var.migration_token
  reconcile_timeout = "15m"
  create_before_destroy = true
  transient_role = "redwood-migrate-iam"
}

Appendix B: useful commands
- KV snapshot: ./bin/kv-backup --target=gs://redwood-migration-backups --consistent
- KV restore: ./bin/kv-restore --source=gs://redwood-migration-backups/snap-20250212 --force-consistent
- Shim dry-run: ./bin/shim-adapter --config=shim.yaml --dry-run --log-format=json
- TF apply with precaution: terraform plan -out tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Appendix C: logs and metrics to collect (for SRE and for customer comms)
- Metrics: runtime.tokens_per_sec, runtime.cache_hit_rate, runtime.kv_restore_time, controlplane.api_5xx_rate, shim.translation_latency_ms
- Logs: controlplane-audit.log, runtime.log (rotate last 10MB), shim-adapter.log (json)

Open questions (for product/PM and security)
- Should we require signed migration_token for every private deployment upgrade (security + audit) or allow short-lived tokens generated by support?
- SLA impact: what is acceptable maintenance window for mid-sized customers (we measured 45–90m end-to-end with manual file transfer).

Next steps and owners
- Maya: land TF wrapper changes and add plan-lock flow (ETA 2026-03-10)
- Devon: prototype KV warmup controller + run env-B replay with 100% traffic (ETA 2026-03-24)
- Aria: expand shim mapping rules and ship sidecar parser for header mappings (ETA 2026-03-17)

Version history
- v0.1 (2025-09-15): initial experimental notes (env-A run)
- v0.6 (2025-12-10): env-B results and TF wrapper iteration
- v1.0-draft (2026-02-28): consolidated checklist, rollback cookbook, automation priorities
